title: Enforce time-based data splitting before modeling future trends
when_to_use: The task requires predicting future trends or evaluating performance over time.
experience:
*   Before any feature engineering or modeling, explicitly define a cutoff date to separate historical data (for feature construction) from future data (for label construction or validation).
*   Verify that the future window has sufficient data coverage for the prediction horizon (e.g., 3-6 months).
*   Ensure no information from after the cutoff date leaks into the feature set (e.g., only use features calculated from data strictly before the cutoff).
*   When evaluating model accuracy, test the model on data from a distinct, out-of-time period that was not used for training.
checklist: Define and document the cutoff date and future window.
Audit features to confirm they are based only on historical data.
Split dataset into training (historical) and testing (future) sets before modeling.
Validate that the test set represents the intended prediction horizon.
common_failure_prevented: Prevents inflated accuracy scores from data leakage and invalidates trend predictions built on non-temporal splits.

title: Construct model evaluation metrics beyond simple accuracy
when_to_use: The task specifies a target model performance (e.g., accuracy >85%).
experience:
*   Use multiple evaluation metrics appropriate for the task (e.g., precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC) to provide a comprehensive performance view.
*   For classification tasks, generate a confusion matrix and calculate metrics for each class, especially the target class (e.g., high-value customers).
*   If the model produces a score, evaluate performance across thresholds (e.g., top-K identification rate) rather than a single threshold.
*   Report results on a properly held-out test set, not on the training data.
checklist: Calculate precision, recall, and F1-score for the target class.
Generate and interpret a confusion matrix.
Plot ROC curve and report AUC if applicable.
Report performance on a separate test set.
common_failure_prevented: Prevents claiming success based on a single, potentially misleading accuracy metric calculated on the wrong data.

title: Define target labels using future outcomes before modeling
when_to_use: The task requires building a model to predict a future state or trend.
experience:
*   Before building a predictive model, operationalize the target variable (label) using data from the *future* period defined in your time split.
*   For trend prediction, define the label as a measurable change (e.g., ratio, classification) between a historical baseline and the future outcome window.
*   Explicitly compute and document the label for each entity in the training set using only post-cutoff data.
*   Ensure the label construction logic is reproducible and matches the business goal (e.g., 'high-value' defined by future revenue, not past behavior).
checklist: Operationalize the prediction target using future-period data.
Define a clear formula or rule for the label (e.g., future value > threshold).
Calculate the label for each entity in the training dataset.
common_failure_prevented: Prevents building models that merely describe current states instead of genuinely predicting future outcomes.
